calls.head: Second night of a back-to-back for the Red Wings
calls.body: The Red Wings played last night and get no rest before this one. Teams in that spot usually get the worse of the chances, so we expect the Canadiens to control more of the play than they usually do.

calls.head: Special teams lean toward the Red Wings
calls.body: The Canadiens’ penalty kill is near the bottom of the league, and the Red Wings’ power play is one of the best. Discipline matters more than usual for the Canadiens tonight. The Canadiens take a lot of penalties and the Red Wings draw plenty of them, so their power play should get its chances.

surprises.head: A big night for Daniil Tarasov
surprises.body: Tarasov stopped all 30 shots, worth 3.6 expected goals, through overtime. Starting goalies have a night this good about once every 200 starts. Most starters don’t get one a season.

story.head: Fowler blanks the Red Wings
paras: No goal counted through overtime. The league looked at a Canadiens chance a little over a minute in on video and ruled no goal. Montréal had what would have been the winner taken off for offside less than three minutes into overtime, but it didn’t cost them in the end. Zachary Bolduc scored the only goal of the shootout for the Canadiens.
Nothing much separated these two on the chances. This one could have gone either way. Jacob Fowler was perfect for the Canadiens, 30 saves on 30 shots, and Daniil Tarasov stopped 30 of 30.
Neither power play scored: the Canadiens killed all four Red Wings power plays, and the Red Wings killed all four of Montréal’s. The Habs improved to 2-2-1, and the Red Wings dropped to 1-3-1.

items.text: The Canadiens won for the first time in four games.
The Canadiens’ Kaiden Guhle played his first game of the season, after missing the first four.
One of the preview’s two calls held.
